title: Wren and the Asset
premise: Wren Villalobos, a burned-out interpreter for a collapsing peace delegation, is approached by a stranger who claims Wren once saved his life—a favor Wren has no memory of. The debt comes due: extract Dr. Ilse Marchetti, a defector carrying proof that the peace talks are a cover for an arms deal, from a city sliding into lockdown. As Wren runs the extraction, he uncovers that the 'incident' that shattered his sleep was erased from his own memory, and that he knew Marchetti before either of them will admit. The defector is bait in a trap set by the delegation's own security chief, and Wren must choose between exposing the truth and protecting the fragile found family of handlers and strays who've gathered around him. In the end, Wren trades his own anonymity—broadcasting the evidence and surrendering himself—to get Marchetti out alive, discovering that the missing memory was his choice to forget, and reclaiming it is how he finally sleeps.
about_author: Ada Halloran is a former NGO field coordinator who spent six years in border towns where every conversation happened twice, once in each language and once in what wasn't said. She writes thrillers about people whose jobs require them to be trusted by strangers.

chapters.title: The Favor That Never Happened
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Insomniac and invisible at the tail end of failed peace talks, Wren is cornered in a hotel bar by Tomas Reyes, who insists Wren pulled him from a burning car in Sarajevo—a night Wren cannot recall. Reyes leaves a keycard and a name: Dr. Ilse Marchetti. The beat is unease: kindness remembered wrong is more frightening than a threat.

chapters.title: Interest Owed
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Investigating the keycard leads to a dead drop and a recording of his own voice speaking a language he shouldn't know. His handler, Priya, warns him to walk away; the delegation is days from collapse and everyone is choosing sides. Wren realizes Marchetti requested him by name. Emotional beat: the vertigo of being a stranger to your own past.

chapters.title: The Woman Who Knew My Voice
chapters.summary: Wren meets Marchetti in the university archive where she's hidden; she greets him with a childhood nickname no one living should know. She carries encrypted proof the peace process launders arms sales, but refuses to move until Wren admits they've met. He can't. Beat: intimacy without memory, trust extended on credit.

chapters.title: Lockdown
chapters.summary: Marchetti's POV. The city seals its borders after a staged bombing; Marchetti navigates checkpoints using forged credentials while observing Wren through surveillance she secretly controls. She recognizes his memory loss as deliberate—she's seen the procedure before. Beat: guilt, as she understands she may be the reason he chose to forget.

chapters.title: Priya's Ledger
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya discovers the delegation's security chief, Brandt, has been feeding Marchetti's location to both sides, playing the defector as bait to flush out leaks—including Wren. She burns her own cover to warn them, joining the extraction rather than reporting it. Beat: loyalty crystallizing into found family under pressure.

chapters.title: The Long Corridor
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. A tense transit through the flooded metro tunnels, evading Brandt's sweep teams, during which Marchetti tells Wren the truth: he volunteered for memory suppression after Sarajevo, where his interpreting was used to lure refugees into an ambush. Beat: grief arriving before the memory itself does.

chapters.title: What Was Taken
chapters.summary: Marchetti's POV. Hiding in a chapel, Marchetti helps Wren trigger fragments of return—the ambush, the child he couldn't save, the choice to erase rather than carry it. Reyes appears: he was the soldier who disobeyed orders that night, and the 'favor' was real, just not the way he told it. Beat: identity rebuilt from wreckage.

chapters.title: Bait
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Brandt corners them at the extraction point with the delegation's remnants as witnesses, offering Wren reinstatement if he hands over Marchetti and the evidence. Wren stalls, buying time while Priya reroutes their escape through the port. Beat: the trap snapping shut—and Wren refusing to flinch.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: Climax, alternating POV. At the harbor, Wren hijacks the delegation's press feed to release Marchetti's evidence live, making himself the story so the escape boat goes unnoticed. Brandt's forces converge; Reyes takes a bullet covering the boarding; Priya pilots them out through the cargo channel. Beat: sacrifice as authorship—one man's voice spent to buy many truths.

chapters.title: Sleep
chapters.summary: Resolution, Wren's POV. Weeks later, in a safehouse north of the border, Wren testifies via deposition while Marchetti rebuilds her life and Priya visits with bad coffee and worse jokes. The memories hurt now instead of haunting. On the first quiet night, Wren sleeps through until morning. Beat: found family as the architecture of recovery; identity chosen, not assigned.
